# Fixture provenance

Every `*-cityparquet/` package here was **generated**, not hand-written: a
CityParquet file is a Parquet file with a `city` key in its footer, and a
hand-rolled one would only ever prove that this reader agrees with itself. They
are written by the reference writer, so a decode bug shows up as a disagreement
with the tool that real files come from.

## Writer

`cityparquet-rs`, built from source and run as its release binary:

```
/data2/hideba/cityparquet-paper/cityparquet-rs/target/release/cityparquet
```

Commit: **`cd8bf69ba63e3929643794589fbfee3f7f1834a6`**
(`git -C /data2/hideba/cityparquet-paper/cityparquet-rs rev-parse HEAD`)

Defaults in force for every invocation below — none were overridden:
`--recipe cityparquet`, `--geometry-encoding wkb`, and LoD0 footprint synthesis
ON. That last one is why the round-trip oracle compares only the LoDs BOTH
models carry: the writer adds an LoD0 footprint the CityJSON sources do not
have.

The CLI is **not** a dependency of this package and is not needed to run the
tests; the generated bytes are committed. Re-generate only when the format or
the writer changes, and re-read the round-trip test when you do.

## Sources and commands

Run from this directory unless noted. `$CLI` is the binary above.

### `two-buildings-cityparquet/` — the main fixture (EPSG:7415)

From `two-buildings.city.json`, itself a copy of the app repo's
`fixtures/two-buildings.city.json` (committed here so the submodule's tests do
not reach into the parent repo):

```bash
"$CLI" convert -o two-buildings-cityparquet --overwrite two-buildings.city.json
```

Yields `building.parquet` (22930 B) + `metadata.json`; 3 objects, LoDs `0.0`
and `2.2`. Footer CRS: `CompoundCRS "Amersfoort / RD New + NAP height"`,
`{"authority":"EPSG","code":7415}`.

### `two-buildings-cityparquet-28992/` — the CRS-disagreement fixture

The SAME geometry with a different declared CRS, so `assembleCityParquetModel`
can be shown to refuse a package whose tables disagree. Produced from an edited
copy of the source — only `metadata.referenceSystem` differs:

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
m = json.load(open("two-buildings.city.json"))
m["metadata"]["referenceSystem"] = "https://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/28992"
json.dump(m, open("/tmp/two-buildings-28992.city.json", "w"))
EOF
"$CLI" convert -o two-buildings-cityparquet-28992 --overwrite /tmp/two-buildings-28992.city.json
```

Yields `building.parquet` (22263 B) + `metadata.json`. Footer CRS:
`ProjectedCRS "Amersfoort / RD New"`, `{"authority":"EPSG","code":28992}` — in
both the `city` and the geoparquet `geo` footer metadata. The edited source is
NOT committed: it is one line away from the one that is, and a second near-copy
of a fixture invites the two to drift.

### `holes-cityparquet/` — the interior-ring fixture

From `holes.city.json` (hand-written here, and committed): one `Building`,
one `Solid` at LoD 2.2, a 10x8 m box 6 m tall whose flat `RoofSurface` is
written in CityJSON's `[[outer], [inner]]` form with a 4x6 m rectangular
opening strictly inside it, coplanar at z = 6 m and wound the opposite way. It
deliberately shares `two-buildings.city.json`'s `transform.scale`
(`[0.001, 0.001, 0.001]`) and its EPSG:7415 `referenceSystem`, so the round-trip
test's 1e-3 quantized coordinate key stays exact.

```bash
"$CLI" convert --output holes-cityparquet --overwrite holes.city.json
```

Yields `building.parquet` (21361 B) + `metadata.json`. It exists because
`two-buildings` cannot fail the hole case: every polygon in it is simply
connected, so a reader that stopped after ring 0 of each WKB polygon would
round-trip it perfectly.

Two things worth knowing about the writer, observed while generating it: the
interior ring survives exactly (ring order, vertex order and winding all come
back as written), and the synthesized LoD0 footprint is the OUTER ring only —
it does not carry the hole down.
